From now on we will not make any distinction between a sheaf on
<MATH_0001> or a sheaf on <MATH_0002>. We will always use the procedures
of the proof of the lemma to go between the two notions.
Next, we establish some relationships between the topoi
associated to these sites.

Let <MATH_0001> be a big Zariski site.
Let <MATH_0002> be a morphism in <MATH_0003>.
The functor <MATH_0004>

<MATH_0005>
For a sheaf <MATH_0006> on <MATH_0007>
we have the formula <MATH_0008>.
The functor <MATH_0009> also has a left adjoint <MATH_0010> which commutes
with fibre products and equalizers.

Denote the functor <MATH_0001>.
In other words, given and open immersion <MATH_0002> corresponding
to an object of <MATH_0003> we set <MATH_0004>.
This functor commutes with fibre products, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Moreover, <MATH_0005> has equalizers (as any two morphisms with the same
source and target are the same) and <MATH_0006> commutes with them.
It is clearly cocontinuous.
It is also continuous as <MATH_0007> transforms coverings to coverings and
commutes with fibre products. Hence the lemma follows from
Sites, Lemmas <REF_0002>
and <REF_0003>.
